text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Belgraders block city streets with their cars in continuation of protests over annulment of election results. Today they will join IN Orthodox Christmas Eve ceremony.
- Students of Nis write to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic reminding him that a long time has passed since he promised to look into complaints over Nis electoral fraud.
- Export-import firm Progres plans to export 10,000 tonnes of corn to Russia despite low price on world market. It will purchase Russian gas and cover the losses.
- Serbian confectionary producer Bambi from Pozarevac plans to increase its exports this year.
- Yugoslav government decided that agricultural producers can purchase certain machinery for commodities, says Yugoslav agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov.
- Yugoslav metallurgy produced 575,000 tonnes of pig iron in 1996 which is 431 percent more than in 1995.
- Nis tobacco industry DIN plans to start discussion on ownership transformation in the spring. DIN to increase production to 13,200 tonnes of cigarettes in 1997.
- Serbians and Montenegrins celebrate Orthodox Christmas Eve today. Patriarch Pavle to hold midnight mass in Belgrade.
- Forensic medicine institute determines heart attack to be cause of death of Predrag Starcevic, demonstrator who died on December 24.
- Pancevo oil refinery processed around two million tonnes of oil in 1996, which is 22 percent above plan.
- Serbia's planned 37 percent of export growth in 1997 is unrealistic, says Momir Pavlicevic, deputy president of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce.
